title: The Young Man Who Gave Up Everything
script: Narrator: [warmly] Before he became a Muslim, Mus'ab ibn Umair was probably the most fashionable young man in all of Makkah.
Narrator: [thoughtful] His family was wealthy, so he always wore the finest clothes and the sweetest perfume that money could buy.
Narrator: [reflective] When he first heard the Prophet's message, he went secretly, because he was afraid of what his family would think.
Narrator: [serious] Although his mother threatened to lock him away, Mus'ab refused to abandon his new faith, no matter what she said.
Narrator: [sadly] Eventually, she stopped feeding him well and took away his comfortable clothes, hoping that hunger would change his mind.
Narrator: [with admiration] It never did. He simply accepted a harder life, since his faith mattered more to him than comfort ever had.
Narrator: [proudly] Later, the Prophet chose him for an important task, sending him to Madinah to teach the new religion there.
Narrator: [thoughtful] This was remarkable, because Mus'ab was young and had no experience teaching anyone, yet he traveled there gladly.
Narrator: [warmly] While he was in Madinah, he taught patiently, and because of his gentle manner, many families accepted Islam that year.
Narrator: [with wonder] People said that when Mus'ab spoke, even skeptical listeners softened, since his sincerity was impossible to ignore or doubt.
Narrator: [serious] Years later, at the Battle of Uhud, Mus'ab carried the Muslim flag and stood firmly beside the Prophet until the end.
Narrator: [tense] When enemies surrounded him, he kept fighting bravely, although he must have known that the danger around him was growing.
Narrator: [sadly] He was killed that day, and when his companions looked for a cloth to bury him, they found only one small piece.
Narrator: [with feeling] It was so small that if they covered his head, his feet showed, and if they covered his feet, his head showed.
Narrator: [reflective] The Prophet wept, remembering the young man who once wore the finest silk, now buried in barely any cloth at all.
Narrator: [warmly] Whenever I think of Mus'ab, I remember that true richness was never about what he owned, but about what he believed.
